newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa OTK says to list, sees higher profits.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa OTK says to list, sees higher profits.

text.p: South Africa's OTK Holdings Ltd, a grain processing and storage firm which will list next week, is expected to raise after-tax profits by 22 percent in the 1996/1997 financial year compared to a year ago, it said on Monday.

Addressing an Investment Analysts Society meeting, financial director De Wet Goosen said OTK, which will debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange next Monday, is seen lifting after tax profits to 186.4 million rand in the year to end February.
This would push earnings to 59.1 cents per combined unit, up from 51.1 cents in the previous year. A combined unit comprises one share worth one cent and one debenture worth 192 cents.
Goosen said the group would list with a market capitalisation of 1.417 billion rand and with a forward price earnings ratio of 7.6, down from 8.8 in 1996.
Mpumalanga-based OTK was last year transformed into a company after operating as an agricultural co-operative since its establishment by a group of farmers in 1923.
Goosen said the pre-listing offer to institutions of shares priced at 310 cents each, was only 26 percent subscribed. The remaining 74 percent of share capital is held by individuals.
Managing director Joos du Plessis said the group was looking to expand through entering into joint ventures with, or buying other companies.
"More than one food and feed company is negotiating with us at this very moment," du Plessis said.
"Talks are advanced. I am positive one or more of these ventures will be successful in the near future."
